title: Upper-valley landslide and a river that moved

story.headline: A river changed course. The cause was a landslide 12 days earlier, 3.8 km upstream
story.context: In remote mountain valleys nobody may see a landslide fall. The first sign downstream is a river that suddenly runs somewhere new, cutting off paths and fields. NISAR passes every 12 days through monsoon cloud, so the radar record can be read backwards like a forensic timeline.
story.radar_insight: Calm water reflects radar away like a mirror (specular reflection), so river channels look dark and a moved channel shows up as a dark line in a new place. A landslide strips forest, dropping the return by several dB, and destroys InSAR coherence between the passes either side of it. In the pass before it failed, InSAR also caught the slope creeping away from the satellite.

sensor.insar_product: NISAR L2 GUNW (geocoded unwrapped interferogram: phase and coherence)

validation.note: Detected landslide area on the latest pass compared with the simulation's own ground truth.
